sections.h2: Where is Brownsburg, Indiana, and how big is it?
sections.html:
Brownsburg is a town in Hendricks County, west of Indianapolis, with an estimated 34,089 residents as of July 1, 2025. Wikipedia lists a 2020 census count of 28,973, up from 21,285 in 2010 and 14,520 in 2000.

That is roughly a doubling in twenty years, and the town covers about 16.4 square miles at an elevation near 879 feet. White Lick Creek, a tributary of the White River, runs north to south just west of the center.

Three out of four homes here are owner-occupied, and households average 2.73 people. A Brownsburg sale is usually a single-family house, not a rental unit, so the questions are about condition, timing and equity.

sections.h2: How did Brownsburg start, and why does the history show up in older houses?
sections.html:
James B. Brown first settled the area in 1824, and the town was founded in 1835 as Harrisburgh. A post office opened in 1836 and took the name Brownsburg because another Indiana county already used the earlier name.

The town was first incorporated in 1848, dissolved during the Civil War, and was incorporated again in 1870. An 1820 road to Indianapolis carried a stagecoach line and brought in settlers.

Most of Brownsburg's housing is far newer than that history, which fits the fast growth since 2000. Any house that predates the recent growth may carry older systems, and a cash sale avoids spending money on updates that a buyer may want to redo. Part of the 1985 film Hoosiers was shot in the former College Avenue Gym, a reminder that the town's center has been around a while.

sections.h2: What roads and jobs shape the Brownsburg housing market?
sections.html:
US 136 is Brownsburg's main east-west road and State Road 267 its main north-south road, and both connect to Interstate 74, which has two nearby interchanges. The town's economic development page also names Ronald Reagan Parkway as the industrial and distribution corridor that links I-74 to I-70 and Indianapolis International Airport.

The same page lists these major employers and local draws:

  • Brunswick, a Fortune 500 company
  • Maplehurst Bakeries
  • LAPP USA, a German-based manufacturer
  • Lucas Oil Indianapolis Raceway Park, which hosts the NHRA U.S. Nationals
  • Three hospitals and a VA clinic

Commuting from Brownsburg runs about 24 minutes on average, per the Census Bureau. Owners who relocate for work usually face tight timelines, and a closing date you set yourself can fit around a new job start.

Source for the roads and employers is the Town of Brownsburg economic development page.

sections.h2: Which school district covers a Brownsburg house?
sections.html:
Brownsburg Community School Corporation serves most of the town, and a small part of Brownsburg falls in the North West Hendricks Schools district, whose high school is Tri-West Hendricks High School. The town's own page describes the Brownsburg district as eleven schools: eight elementary schools, two middle schools and one high school.

Buyers with children often start their search with the district line, so confirm which district your address is in before you list it. A house in the smaller district may need a different explanation to a buyer. Private options include Bethesda Christian School and St. Malachy Catholic School.

Schools matter less to a cash investor than to an owner-occupant, and that is one reason some sellers who are relocating or settling an estate choose to skip the listing.

sections.h2: What permits and flood rules apply to Brownsburg property?
sections.html:
Brownsburg uses an online permit portal, and the Development Services Department oversees planning and building. The Advisory Plan Commission reviews new development, and the Board of Zoning Appeals hears requests to vary standards such as setbacks. The town hall address is 61 N. Green St., and the phone listed for these questions is (317) 858-6072.

Floodplain rules sit in Chapter 152 of the town code. The Floodplain Administrator inspects work in progress, can issue a written stop-work notice, and can revoke a permit tied to false statements. Records are public at Town Hall.

  • If you have unpermitted work, such as a finished basement or a deck, expect questions from buyers.
  • If your lot is near White Lick Creek, check floodplain status before you assume a clean sale.
  • If you inherited a house, find out whether open permits exist before closing.

The town code, Chapter 152 has the enforcement language.

sections.h2: How do Hendricks County property taxes affect a Brownsburg sale?
sections.html:
Hendricks County property tax is due in two installments, the standard Indiana dates being May 10 and November 10. The state's Department of Local Government Finance lists a 5 percent penalty if you pay within 30 days of the due date and a 10 percent penalty after that.

The Town of Brownsburg points owners to the Hendricks County Auditor's website for property values, sale history and tax details. Pull your parcel record before you accept any offer, so you know what the tax bill has been. Property tax bills in Indiana arrive in spring, and the title company handles the proration at closing.

See the state due dates page and the town planning and building page.

sections.h2: What do parks and local services add to a Brownsburg home?
sections.html:
The town economic development page reports over 300 acres of parkland, four developed parks and 20 miles of trails. It also says three hospitals and a VA clinic serve the area.

These details help a buyer picture daily life, and they are worth mentioning to anyone you talk to about your house. They do not change what condition the roof or furnace is in, which is what drives a cash offer.

The town's own page reports a 99% graduation rate for the school district and says 50% of residents hold a bachelor's degree or higher. Those are the town's figures, so treat them as promotional context.

sections.h2: What does a cash sale look like in Brownsburg?
sections.html:
You tell us about the house, we review it, and if you accept the offer we close with a local title company on a date you choose. There is no lender, so there is no loan approval step that can fall through.

Many Brownsburg sellers own a house they bought during the growth years and now want to move on without staging, showings or a listing agreement. Others inherit a house in Hendricks County and live far away, so a single closing by mail or remote signing is easier than managing a listing. Typical Brownsburg situations include:

  • Owners moving for work on short notice
  • Inherited homes with unknown repair needs
  • Houses with deferred maintenance after long ownership
  • Owners behind on payments who want to avoid foreclosure

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Brownsburg, Indiana?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau lists $309,400 as the median value of owner-occupied housing units for 2020 to 2024. Your own number depends on size, condition and location, so treat the figure as a general reference only.

faqs.q: Which school district is Brownsburg in?
faqs.a: Most of the town is in Brownsburg Community School Corporation. A small part is in North West Hendricks Schools, which feeds Tri-West Hendricks High School. Check your address with the district.

faqs.q: When are Hendricks County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Indiana's standard dates are May 10 and November 10, moved to the next business day if they land on a weekend or holiday. Penalties are 5 percent within 30 days and 10 percent after that.

faqs.q: Does Brownsburg have flood rules for homes?
faqs.a: Yes. Chapter 152 of the town code covers flood hazard areas and gives the Floodplain Administrator power to inspect work, issue stop-work notices and revoke permits. Records are available at Town Hall, 61 N. Green St.

faqs.q: How long does it take to close on a Brownsburg house?
faqs.a: The timeline is your choice within reason. With no lender, closing depends mostly on how fast the title company completes its search and paperwork, and we can work around your move date.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Brownsburg house if it needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. We buy houses as-is, so you do not need to fix the roof, finish unpermitted work or update the kitchen before an offer.
